ACID Transactions

1. What are Ignite Transactions?
  • Ignite supports fully ACID-compliant distributed transactions across multiple keys, caches, and partitions;
  • Atomicity — all operations in a transaction succeed or all are rolled back;
  • Consistency — the cluster moves from one valid state to another;
  • Isolation — concurrent transactions don't see each other's uncommitted changes;
  • Durability — committed transactions survive node failures (when persistence is enabled);
2. When can you use Transactions?
  • The cache must have atomicityMode = TRANSACTIONAL: 
    CacheConfiguration cfg = new CacheConfiguration("myCache");
cfg.setAtomicityMode(CacheAtomicityMode.TRANSACTIONAL);
  • ATOMIC caches do not support multi-key transactions (each operation is independently atomic);
  • You can span a single transaction across multiple TRANSACTIONAL caches;
3. Basic Transaction Usage
  • try (Transaction tx = ignite.transactions().txStart()) {
    Integer balance = cache.get("account-A");
    cache.put("account-A", balance - 100);
    cache.put("account-B", cache.get("account-B") + 100);

    tx.commit();
} catch (Exception e) {
    // Transaction is automatically rolled back when the try block exits without commit
}
  • If tx.commit() is not called, the transaction is rolled back automatically;
4. Transaction with Specific Settings
  • try (Transaction tx = ignite.transactions().txStart(
        TransactionConcurrency.PESSIMISTIC,
        TransactionIsolation.REPEATABLE_READ,
        10_000,  // timeout in ms
        0        // max size (0 = unlimited)
)) {
    // transactional operations...
    tx.commit();
}
5. Two-Phase Commit (2PC)
  • Ignite uses a two-phase commit protocol for distributed transactions:
    1. Prepare phase — all participating nodes acquire locks and verify the transaction can succeed;
    2. Commit phase — if all nodes voted "yes", the transaction is committed on all nodes;
  • If any node votes "no" in the prepare phase, the entire transaction is rolled back;
6. Transaction Timeout
  • Set a timeout to prevent transactions from holding locks forever: 
    // Per transaction
ignite.transactions().txStart(PESSIMISTIC, REPEATABLE_READ, 5000, 0);

// Default for all transactions
TransactionConfiguration txCfg = new TransactionConfiguration();
txCfg.setDefaultTxTimeout(10_000);
igniteCfg.setTransactionConfiguration(txCfg);
  • Timed-out transactions are automatically rolled back;
